verses.1: And when King Hizkia heard this, he cut his clothes in half and covered himself with a cloak. Then he went into the house of Jehovah.
verses.2: And he sent Eljakim, who was responsible for the house, as well as Shabna, the scribe, and the elders of the priests, all wearing their robes, to go to Yeshua son of Amos, the prophet.
verses.3: And they said to him, “Thus says Hizkiah: ‘Today will be a day of disaster and destruction. Today, children will be born with weakness and lack of strength.’”
verses.4: But may Jehovah your God hear the words of the king of Assyria, who has sent his messengers to mock God. May He confirm His words by what Jehovah your God hears. And may you pray for those who remain in captivity.
verses.5: And the servants of King Hizkiah went to Yeshua.
verses.6: And He said to them, “Yishayahu, say this to your people: ‘The LORD says, do not be afraid of what the sons of King Ashur have said against me.’”
verses.7: I will give him breath and hearing, and he will return to his land. Then I will throw him down in the valley of his own land.
verses.8: And Rab-shakhe sat down and found that the king of Assyria was fighting against Lebanon. He heard that the king of Israel had left.
verses.9: And King Kush heard of this. He said, “I will go and fight against you.” So he sent servants to Hizkiah, saying, “Come here.”
verses.10: So say to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, “Do not trust in your God, whom you rely on. Do not give Jerusalem into the hands of the king of Assyria.”
verses.11: Now, you have heard that the kings of Assyria have decreed a ban on all nations. And you will be punished for this.
verses.12: They were saved by the gods of those nations who corrupted my ancestors—Gozan, Haran, Rezef, and the sons of Edan, who were destroyed.
verses.13: May the king of Hamath, the king of Arphad, and the king of the city of Sefarvaim be destroyed and defeated.
verses.14: And Hizkiah took the books from the hands of the scribes. He read them out loud before Jehovah.
verses.15: And Hizkiah prayed to the LORD, saying:
verses.16: Yehovah, the army of heaven, God of Israel! You who sit upon the throne! You alone are the true God, for all kings of the earth. You created the heavens and the earth.
verses.17: May the LORD listen to you! May He open your eyes and see everything that Sanherib has said. He was sent by God to cause destruction.
verses.18: Indeed, Jehovah destroyed the kings of Assyria and their entire land.
verses.19: And they put their gods into fire, because those gods were not real gods at all. They were merely creations of human hands—wood and stone. And so they were destroyed.
verses.20: And now, LORD our God, save us from His hand. Then all the kings of the earth will know that YOU, LORD, are the only one who can save us.
verses.21: And Esaiah son of Amoz was sent to Hezekiah, with these words: “As the LORD, the God of Israel, has said to me: ‘Go to Assyria and speak to the king of Assyria.’”
verses.22: This is what the LORD has said about it: “It will bring you shame and reproach, in the time of Zion’s destruction. The head of Jerusalem will be turned into a pile of ruins.”
verses.23: To whom have you brought shame and disgrace? To whom have you raised your voice in anger? May your eyes be turned towards the Holy Israel.
verses.24: In the hands of your servants, you will be humiliated, O Lord. I have climbed up from the heights of the mountains; I have walked along their paths. I pick the fruits from their branches. I come from the depths of the forest.
verses.25: I have waded and drunk water. Then, with a quick movement of my hand, I have freed all the days in that prison.
verses.26: You have not heard of her from afar. I created her in ancient times. Now, bring her here, so that she can carry the messages of the Lord to the people in various places.
verses.27: And their seats were covered with leaves and thorns. There were also fields of crops, and trees and bushes.
verses.28: And your going back and forth, I know it. And I also know how you’re upset with me.
verses.29: Because you were angered by me, and I heard your words. I placed my hands on your shoulders, and I spoke to you through your lips. I will bring you back on the path you came from.
verses.30: And in that year, they planted vines. In the second year, they harvested them. In the third year, they sowed seeds and planted them as fruit trees. Then they ate their fruits.
verses.31: And the descendants of the House of Judah, who remained at the bottom, became fruitful at the top.
verses.32: For from Jerusalem will come out those who are exiled and oppressed. From the Valley of Hinnom, God’s army will do this.
verses.33: Therefore, as Jehovah said to the king of Assyria: “Do not come into this city. Do not set up walls there. Do not build defenses against it. And do not throw stones on it.”
verses.34: In the time when he will return, and to this city, the Lord will not come.
verses.35: And I will destroy this city, so that it may be saved for Me and for David, My servant.
verses.36: And the angel of the LORD went out and struck down in the camp of Assyria a hundred and seventy-five thousand men. In the morning, they all died.
verses.37: And he went and settled in Sanherib’s kingdom. He ruled over Nineveh.
verses.38: And he became the king of Nisroch, Elah, and Edom. His sons were destroyed in battle. They fled to the land of Aram. And Esar-hadon became their king under his rule.
